newsitem.title: UK: Frontline seeks to issue 25 mln more shares.
newsitem.headline: Frontline seeks to issue 25 mln more shares.

text.p: Oslo-listed tanker operator Frontline Ltd said on Thursday it would seek permission to issue an extra 25 million shares to finance possible future expansion.
The Bermuda-registered company said the move would give it additional flexibility.
"There are currently no specific plans for the issuance of these shares, but the shares will be reserved in order to equity finance further expansion of the company," it said.

Frontline said it would seek permission to issue the shares at an extraordinary meeting in Bermuda on August 14. The meeting, originally scheduled for late July, was called to consider a previously announced placing of 10 million new shares with four new investors.
The meeting would also consider approving an increase in the maximum size of the board from four to eight.

The private placement of 10 million shares was priced at 28.15 crowns per share, the July 10 price of the stock on the Oslo Stock exchange. The company's share price has since risen to trade at 33.7 crowns today.

Frontline said the Bermuda meeting would "consider, and if thought fit approve, an increase in the authorised share capital of the Company from $98.6 million to $133.6 million by the creation of an additional 35 million ordinary shares of par value $1.00 each."
Hemen Holding, which currently owns about 63 percent of shares in Frontline, has undertaken to vote in favour of the issue, the company said. -Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. fax 5017.
